items.title: Section: Clinging to Body and World, and Six Applications That Cure Them

items.zh: 保著內身者，由於生死無厭患門。保著外境者，於未來境由欣樂門。當知此中，為欲對治初隨煩惱故，修一作意，謂正知作意。為欲對治第二隨煩惱故，修三作意。謂稱順彼所緣作意；了別彼相，能對治彼尋思作意；彼所依心調練作意。為欲對治第三隨煩惱故，應修分析積聚作意。為欲對治第四隨煩惱故，應當修習不淨作意。
items.en: Clinging to the inner body arises through the gateway of finding no weariness with birth and death. Clinging to outer objects arises through the gateway of delighting in future objects. To counter the first secondary affliction, one cultivates one mental application, the application of right knowing. To counter the second, one cultivates three applications: the application matching the object, the application discerning its signs to counter deliberation, and the application training the underlying mind. To counter the third, one should cultivate the application of analysing aggregation. To counter the fourth, one should cultivate the application of impurity.

items.title: Section: What Each Application Actually Cures, Down to the Four Kinds of Sexual Desire

items.zh: 又初作意修習、多修習故，能斷忘念。第二作意修習、多修習故，能斷保著內身、外境二種貪欲。第三作意修習、多修習故，能斷惡見等所有散亂。第四作意修習、多修習故，能斷先所串習勢力任持所有散亂。第五作意修習、多修習故，能斷於身淨有情想。第六作意修習、多修習故，能斷四貪。所謂色貪、觸貪、形貪，及承事貪。
items.en: Cultivating and repeatedly cultivating the first application cuts off forgotten mindfulness. Cultivating the second cuts off both cravings, for the inner body and outer objects. Cultivating the third cuts off all distraction rooted in wrong view and the like. Cultivating the fourth cuts off distraction sustained by prior habituation. Cultivating the fifth cuts off the perception of the body as pure and as a sentient being. Cultivating the sixth cuts off four cravings: craving for complexion, for touch, for form, and for being attended upon.

items.title: Section: Touching Genuine Concentration, and Knowing Impermanence Rightly

items.zh: 如是作意修習為依，斷隨煩惱，心觸正定，證得近分、根本勝定，又能證得有喜、離喜、清淨安樂。又依如是正定心故，如實了知上地有情無常性，及諸行無常性。
items.en: Relying on the cultivation of these mental applications, the secondary afflictions are cut off, the mind touches genuine concentration, and both threshold and root excellent absorptions are attained, along with bliss accompanied by joy, bliss with joy left behind, and pure, still bliss. Relying further on this genuinely settled mind, one truly knows the impermanent nature of beings in the higher realms, and the impermanent nature of all conditioned formations.

items.title: Section: Seeing Impermanence with the Divine Eye, and the Threefold Basis of Practice

items.zh: 云何了知有情無常性？謂得天眼，清淨過人，見諸有情，乃至廣說。云何了知諸行無常性？謂能隨入未來、過去、現在作意緣生智故。此隨身念依於三處。謂依增上心、增上慧學修治業地，依增上心學處，依增上慧學處。為欲斷除所餘諸結，修念住等所有一切菩提分法之所依止。
items.en: What is right knowing of a being's impermanent nature? Attaining the divine eye, a purity surpassing the ordinary, one sees beings, as extensively explained. What is right knowing of formations' impermanent nature? Being able to move through future, past, and present, giving rise to the wisdom of dependent origination. This mindfulness carried with the body depends on three bases: the cultivating ground of the higher training in mind and higher training in wisdom, the basis of the higher training in mind, and the basis of the higher training in wisdom. These serve to cut off remaining fetters, and are what the four foundations of mindfulness and every factor of awakening depend upon.

items.title: Section: What Sets Buddhist Practice Apart, and Four Fruits of Complete Requisites

items.zh: 由三因緣，不與一切外道沙門、婆羅門共。謂於修治業地資糧圓滿故；於奢摩他聚無有愛味故；於般涅槃愛樂隨逐心，非煩惱火所生處故。又此修念資糧圓滿為依止故，四果清淨。謂處聚落，世法所生煩惱不染；處阿練若，空閑所生煩惱不染；處阿練若，聚落所生煩惱不染；於二處所，不能堪忍淋漏等苦煩惱不染。
items.en: Through three causes, this is not shared with any non-Buddhist renunciant or brahmin: the requisites of the cultivating ground are complete; there is no craving whatsoever for the calm-abiding attained; and the mind aspires towards nirvana, which is not the birthplace of affliction's own fire. Relying on the completeness of these requisites for cultivating mindfulness, four fruits of purity result: remaining unstained by the affliction that worldly conditions produce while in a village; remaining unstained by the affliction that solitude produces in the wilderness; remaining unstained regardless of either setting; and remaining unstained by the affliction of being unable to bear hardships such as a leaking roof in either setting.

items.title: Section: Five Fruits Free of Craving, Nine Fruits That Follow the Wish for Nirvana

items.zh: 奢摩他聚無有愛味為依止故，五果清淨。謂四種清淨靜慮，及寂靜解脫。於般涅槃愛樂隨逐，心非煩惱火所生處為依止故，九果清淨。謂初三果及六神通。此隨身念，當知五種清淨所攝。
items.en: Relying on freedom from craving towards the calm-abiding attained, five fruits of purity result: the four pure absorptions, and the peaceful liberation of the formless attainments. Relying on the mind's sustained aspiration towards nirvana, which is not the birthplace of affliction's fire, nine fruits of purity result: the first three noble fruits, and the six higher forms of direct knowledge. This mindfulness carried with the body should be known as comprised of five kinds of purity.

items.title: Section: Five Kinds of Purity Gathered Together, and a Second Sutra Opens

items.zh: 謂不定地清淨故、定地清淨故、攝清淨故、不共清淨故、不共果清淨故。又隨逐身轉故，彼所攝受故，名隨身念。復次，當釋摩訶俱瑟祉羅經。有二解脫。一、慧解脫，二、心解脫。
items.en: Namely purity of the ground even without concentration, purity of the ground of concentration, purity of what is gathered, purity not shared with others, and purity of fruits not shared with others. Because it follows the body's own turning, and body and mind are embraced by it, it is named mindfulness carried with the body. The Mahā-Koṭṭhita Sutra shall now be explained. There are two kinds of liberation: liberation through wisdom, and liberation of mind.

items.title: Section: Mundane Wisdom, Mundane Mind, and the Fruit They Share

items.zh: 此中依慧解脫，謂世間慧之所行者，當知即是建立惡行及與善行并彼因緣。彼體性者，當知即是惡行、善行并彼因緣，善不善等體性差別如實正智。又依心解脫，謂心染淨之所依者，當知即是色等境界能取了別。
items.en: Among these, regarding wisdom-liberation, the scope of worldly wisdom is establishing unwholesome and wholesome conduct together with their causes. Its essence is the wisdom that truly knows, as they actually are, the distinct natures of what is wholesome and unwholesome, together with unwholesome and wholesome conduct and their causes. Regarding mind-liberation, that mind is the very basis of defilement and purity means that it is mind which takes in and discerns objects of form and the rest.

items.title: Section: What Wisdom Truly Knows — the Four Noble Truths Themselves

items.zh: 彼世間慧心解脫果，當知即是於彼相應、相雜下類雜染出故。即慧解脫增上力故，出世間慧之所行者，當知即是由世間慧及心解脫增上力故，如實了知一切境界。即出世慧心解脫果，當知即是一切種類雜染出故。此中若世間慧、若出世慧、總略為一，說名正見。
items.en: The fruit of mundane wisdom and mind-liberation is being freed from the defilement of the lowest class, the desire realm, both what is associated with mind and what is intermingled with affliction as its object. Through the enhancing power of wisdom-liberation, the scope of transcendent wisdom is truly knowing every object as it is, through the enhancing power of mundane wisdom and mind-liberation. Among these, whether mundane wisdom or transcendent wisdom, both are, in brief, together called right view.

blocks.text: How mindfulness of the body cures attachment to body and world, and what distinguishes Buddhist meditation.

Master Cháng Bǎi: always knowing whether one's actions accord with the Dharma prevents breaking precepts through lost mindfulness. Analyse the body as earth, water, fire, and wind, and mind as feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness.
Craving for complexion, for soft touch, for shape, and for attentive service. Master Cháng Bǎi: the nine stages of settling the mind cure distraction.
Master Cháng Bǎi: from the first to the fourth meditation; then at will one recalls the past and considers the future, seeing all as conditioned.

subs.head: What sets the Buddha's teaching apart

blocks.text: Master Cháng Bǎi: disciples do not relish the meditations they gain; outsiders often become attached to theirs. Though living in a village, the disciple is not moved by the eight worldly conditions.
Master Cháng Bǎi: only arhats gain the power of ending outflows, so the four fruits and six powers go together.
Master Cháng Bǎi: truly knowing good and evil causes and results is its essence. Worldly right view leaves desire-realm desire and reaches meditation.
"Disciples do not relish the meditations they gain." What makes meditation Buddhist is not technique but the absence of clinging to its results.

quiz.q: What applications counter the first and the fourth secondary afflictions?
options: analysing aggregation for the first, and right knowing for the fourth
impurity for the first, analysing aggregation for the fourth
the application matching the object for both
right knowing for the first, and impurity for the fourth
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: always knowing whether one's three kinds of action accord with Dharma prevents breaking precepts through lost mindfulness; contemplation of impurity counters attachment to outer objects. The third affliction takes analysis of aggregation.

quiz.q: How is the application of analysing aggregation practised, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: dividing one's property and giving it away to break the habit of hoarding
counting breaths to ten and starting over
analysing form as gathered from the elements and mind from feeling and the rest, seeing the body as unreal and selfless
visualising the Buddha's thirty-two marks
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: analyse the inner body's form as gathered from earth, water, fire, and wind, and mind as gathered from feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness; see the body as unreal and selfless. This counters clinging to the inner body.

quiz.q: Which four cravings does the sixth application cut off?
options: sense craving, form craving, formless craving, and craving for existence
craving for wealth, sex, fame, and food
craving for complexion, touch, form, and being attended upon
craving of view, pride, doubt, and delusion
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: craving for fair complexion, for soft smooth touch, for shape and build, and for attentive service. The treatise gives the names only; how each impurity contemplation matches them differs in the sources and is not tested.

quiz.q: What does the fifth application cut off, and what does the fourth, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: the fifth cuts the idea of the body as a pure being; the fourth, the nine stages, cuts habitual distraction
the fifth cuts seeds of the three poisons, the fourth cuts errors of view
the fifth cuts forgetting, the fourth cuts clinging to the body
the fifth cuts four cravings, the fourth wrong view
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the fifth cuts the notion that one's body is a pure being; the fourth is the nine stages of settling the mind, which cut distraction carried along by past habituation. Forgetting belongs to the first, and four cravings to the sixth.

quiz.q: After the secondary afflictions are cut off through these applications, what is attained?
options: immediate arhatship and final exit from the three realms
immediate attainment of the five powers
the mind touches concentration, attaining threshold and root absorptions, with bliss with joy, without it, and pure
immediate attainment of non-retrogression
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one attains threshold concentrations or root absorptions from the first to the fourth meditation. Matching joy and its absence to each meditation follows the 《披尋記》 and is his reading, not a statement of the treatise.

quiz.q: This is rendered "Being able to move through future, past, and present." What is lost?
options: 作意: the wisdom comes from attending to the three times, not from moving among them
nothing: it is a power of travelling through time, linked with the divine eye, as the lecture says
過去 is lost
現在 is lost
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: at will one recalls the past, considers the future, and enters the present, seeing all as conditioned; through this attention one penetrates the wisdom of dependent origination. The English reads like a time-travelling power.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain the second cause by which this is not shared with outsiders?
options: there is no craving for the meditations gained, whereas outsiders often grow attached to them
outsiders cannot attain any meditation at all, only the Buddha's disciples can
outsiders keep no precepts, while disciples do
outsiders do not give, while disciples do
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: disciples have no love or relish for the meditations gained, whereas outsiders often grow attached to theirs. So outsiders can attain meditation; what differs is attachment. He adds that they take meditation for nirvana.

quiz.q: With complete requisites as the basis, four fruits of purity result. Which is one of them?
options: dwelling in a village and converting everyone without falling back
gaining six powers in the wilderness
realising nirvana without residue in both settings
remaining unstained by the affliction worldly conditions produce while in a village
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: though dwelling in a village, the afflictions arising from the eight worldly conditions, gain and loss, fame and blame, praise and censure, pleasure and pain, do not stain one's mind. Six powers belong to another list.

quiz.q: With no craving for calm-abiding as basis, which five fruits of purity result?
options: the first three fruits and six powers, the same contents under another number
the five powers
the five noble treasures
the four pure absorptions and the peaceful liberation
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the five are the four pure meditations plus the peaceful liberation of the four formless attainments. Note that the fifth counts the formless attainments as one. The first three fruits and six powers are the nine that follow.

quiz.q: The treatise lists the first three fruits and six powers. What does Master Cháng Bǎi infer? (This is the lecture's inference, not the treatise's.)
options: six powers should read five, the first three fruits lacking that power, so the text must be emended
nine should be changed to ten, naming arhatship
since only arhats gain the power of ending outflows, the four fruits are in fact included
the first three fruits should mean the four paths
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the fourth fruit is not stated, only six powers, but only arhats gain the power of ending outflows, so in fact the four fruits and six powers can be attained. He does not change the treatise's number. It is an inference, not its wording.

quiz.q: This is rendered "Because it follows the body's own turning and is embraced by it." What is reversed?
options: the relation: body and mind are gathered by mindfulness, not mindfulness by the body
nothing: mindfulness rests upon the body and is held by it, as the lecture explains, so the wording stands
it should be "following the mind"
"turning" should be deleted
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: it follows the practitioner's body and mind as they move, and the body and mind are gathered by mindfulness of the five purities. This is the second reason for the name, and the English has the direction backward.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi divide the scope and essence of worldly wisdom, and what does mind rest upon?
options: the scope is suchness, the essence non-conceptual wisdom, resting on nirvana
the scope is the aggregates, the essence impermanence, resting on the body
the scope is good and evil conduct and causes, the essence is true knowing of them, and the mind king underlies defilement and purity
the scope is the truths, the essence selflessness, resting on precepts
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: worldly good and evil conduct and their causes are its scope; truly knowing good and evil causes and results is its essence. The basis of defilement and purity is the mind king. Suchness as scope belongs to transcendent wisdom.

quiz.q: This is rendered "the desire realm's own lowest class of defilement." What is wrong with 下類?
options: nothing: the realm's afflictions have three grades and only the lowest is left, as the lecture divides
下類 should mean the hells
下類 should mean the form realm
下類 is the desire realm itself, not the lowest group within it
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one leaves the bonds of the low desire realm. Worldly right view leaves desire-realm desire and afflictions and attains meditation. The whole realm is meant, since the desire realm is the lowest of three, not the lowest class within it.
